Open • FLYBYME (Tim) opened about 1 hour ago • 0 comments
Labels: package


  Three things in  mesh-core , batched, ending in the thing that was actually 
  asked for: "i think we need to get me a ui for creating/editing sites and   
  releases and the catalog thing."                                            
                                                                              
  --------                                                                    
                                                                              
  ## 1. Regenerate the client — it currently lies                             
                                                                              
   src/generated/api.ts  documents every call as  auth: public . The console  
  site's                                                                      
  own row declares  auth: 'user'  for all eighteen of its contracts except    
   identity.ticket_issue , and the server agrees with the row:                
                                                                              
    $ curl 'http://127.0.0.1:5005/api/parts?limit=2' -H 'Host: console.       
  localhost'                                                                  
    {"error":"UNAUTHENTICATED","message":"part.find requires a valid ticket."}
                                                                              
  So the one artifact a developer reads to find out whether a call needs      
  authentication says the opposite of the truth. mesh-serve now emits the gate
  as                                                                          
  runtime data rather than a JSDoc comment (FLYBYME/mesh-serve#1, merged), so 
  regenerating both fixes the lie and gives the client something it can act   
  on.                                                                         
                                                                              
  Regenerate, and check the diff rather than trusting it: this is where a     
  stale                                                                       
  lockfile shows up.                                                          
                                                                              
  ## 2. A form vocabulary in  ui                                              
                                                                              
   ui@0.1.0  answers the display half —  entityList ,  entityItem ,           
   detailSurface ,  propertyGrid ,  table ,  tableRow  — and has no way to    
  enter                                                                       
  a record: no field, no label, no select, no button row, no dialog. So the   
  site                                                                        
  editor below either re-opens the hole  ui  was built to close, or it gets   
  built                                                                       
  on something.                                                               
                                                                              
  Write it against a JSON Schema, not against the screens.  GET /api/_describe
  now serves  input  and  output  per exposed call, and the kernel can fetch  
  it                                                                          
  (mesh-web 0.15.5). There are ~154 addressable CRUD contracts in mesh-serve, 
  every                                                                       
  one with both schemas, and zero hand-written UI for any of them.            
                                                                              
  Read  mesh-web/spec/schema-driven-ui.md  §3.2 and §4 first. Two things it   
  makes                                                                       
  binding:                                                                    
                                                                              
  • Do not reinvent settled conventions. The dispatcher listens for  input ,  
  not  change  (a form whose button is clicked from a focused field must still
  see the last keystroke — the classic dropped password). An empty number     
  field                                                                       
  is  undefined , not  0 .  Props = Reactive<Json> | undefined  — a value or a
  getter, never a callback.                                                   
  • The override seam ships in the first commit. Generic by default, refined  
  per contract, refining fields rather than replacing the form. Without it,   
  the first screen with real requirements hand-writes its form and then every 
  screen does. This is the  defaultFrame  shape: the ordinary thing, with     
  every                                                                       
  piece overridable.                                                          
                                                                              
  ## 3. The site editor                                                       
                                                                              
  The thing that was asked for. Point it at  site  first: a real  defineCrud ,
   scopedBy: tenantId , and the reads are already exposed.                    
                                                                              
  One blocker you will hit immediately: every write is internal. There is no  
  exposed  site.create  or  site.update ; the only writes reachable from a    
  browser                                                                     
  are  cdn.compose  and  cdn.deploy . That is a mesh-serve change, not yours —
  open an issue for it, linked, and state the shape it needs:                 
                                                                              
  │  site.contract.ts  says  update  stays internal "because which release a  
  │ hostname serves is  cdn.deploy 's business." That reasoning is right for  
  │  releaseHash  and wrong for  theme ,  policy ,  title ,  indexable  and   
  the                                                                         
  │  mesh  exposure list. The split is to expose  create  and  update  with   
  │  releaseHash  excluded from the update input, so editing a site and       
  │ deploying a release stay two different acts.                              
                                                                              
  Until that lands, build the editor against the reads and the two writes that
  do                                                                          
  exist, and make the disabled parts visibly disabled rather than broken.     
                                                                              
  Note the composition already runs  chrome , so this is a window in an       
  existing                                                                    
  console, not a new site.

    Desired and observed sit next to each other on every row and are never merged.

    and what it is running, and showing both says more than a flag could. A row that
    reads '2 running, 3 assigned' with 'not running: builder' underneath is the
    whole diagnosis.
    
    One node.status call covers the table -- it returns a summary for every node --
    rather than one observed lookup per machine, which would be seven round trips
    arriving at different times and flickering between disagreeing states.
